biased_opinion.summary: Muck n Mac Fest combines two substantial Scottish Borders gravel days with timed enduro segments, transfers, camping, and a festival at Traquair House. The venue and format lift the experience, while regional field depth and limited prestige keep it in Tier 4.
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A distinctive Scottish gravel weekender for riders who want racing, transfers, camping, and festival time in one package.

final_verdict.one_liner: Two Borders gravel days with the clock running only when it matters.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race it if a social two-day gravel enduro and festival is more appealing than one continuous mass-start sufferfest.

logistics.explanation: Lexi Ligeti calls it "extremely well organised" and Mark praises "clean toilets and hot showers" in the event village. Free camping is included with weekend tickets, but the research provides no airport access, parking details, or packet pickup information. Multiple riders return annually, suggesting the basics work despite thin logistical transparency.

length.explanation: The organizer's 2027 Long Weekender is approximately 75 km on both Saturday and Sunday, or roughly 150 km total, with untimed transfers between timed stages. Mark notes you can "take twice as long to get value for money" in the enduro format. The two-day structure rewards repeatability and recovery more than one continuous ultra-distance effort.

technicality.explanation: Routes mix "technical single tracks, endless forest trails, country roads" through 65% gravel and 35% tarmac terrain. Craig M noted he "underestimated area for gravel riding" in the Tweed Valley. The course includes "muddy forest trails, technical tracks" but welcomes adaptive cyclists, suggesting moderate technical demands rather than expert-level features. Less technical than The Mid South.

elevation.explanation: The organizer's current Long Weekender description uses more than 3,000 m across two days as the planning baseline, with steep gradients, ancient woodland, and moorland passes. Exact 2027 gain remains unpublished and is deliberately not presented as a verified edition figure.

climate.explanation: May dates in the Scottish Borders carry weather uncertainty, and the event name "Muck n Mac" explicitly references mud conditions. The terrain includes "muddy forest trails" and "remote forest roads" that would amplify weather impacts. No historical weather data available, but organizers clearly design around wet Scottish spring conditions. More weather exposure than Belgian Waffle Ride San Diego.

altitude.explanation: Traquair House sits in the Tweed Valley at river elevation with routes through "ancient woodlands" rather than high country. The Scottish Borders location offers rolling hills without meaningful altitude effects. Maximum elevations aren't specified, confirming this isn't mountain terrain. Lower altitude than Gravel Worlds — no thin-air concerns.

adventure.explanation: Riders explore "remote forest roads, flowing gravel descents, and hidden singletrack" around Scotland's oldest inhabited house with 900-year history. The grounds include ancient yew trees, Bear Gates closed since 1745, and access to the UK's oldest operating brewery. Lorna M loved the "wonderful chilled and friendly atmosphere" at this historic venue.

prestige.explanation: The sixth edition in 2027 is established enough to have a repeat community but remains a regional Scottish festival rather than a destination pro race. No elite field or notable winners are promoted, and full-weekend riding is capped at 400 entries.

race_quality.explanation: Caroline H "wasn't sure about the timed stages format but actually really enjoyed it" in the gravel enduro structure. Community ratings show 4.4/5 overall with high marks for event logistics (4.71/5) and safety (4.79/5). Course navigation scored 4.12/5, indicating solid execution of a still-evolving format.

experience.explanation: Gillian H returns for her "3rd year" calling it "a highlight of our busy calendar." The weekend includes ceilidh dancing, live music, outdoor yoga, and breathwork sessions beyond riding. Angela L praised "fantastic scenery and a great mixture of trails" with good camping amenities, though aid stations scored lower at 3.87/5.

community.explanation: 87% of reviewers describe the atmosphere as "Small & Intimate" rather than large festival scale. Bob G "LOVED the ceilidh" and praised the "lovely people" in the 400-rider field. Free entry for kids under 14 with bike activities creates family appeal, but the community remains small and regionally focused.

field_depth.explanation: The organizer caps full-weekend riding at 400 entries and day-only riding at 50 entries per day. No elite field or notable racers are promoted. Al C describes "friendly staff" and Mark notes it works for "pros and people like me who take twice as long," confirming participation-focused rather than elite depth.

value.explanation: The first 100 2027 Full Weekender entries are listed at £110 and include two marked ride days, timing, both GPX files, camping, showers, parking, and festival access. You're paying for the complete weekend rather than only a start number.

expenses.explanation: The current early Full Weekender price is £110. The Scottish Borders location is roughly 1.5 hours from Edinburgh; included camping, parking, and showers control accommodation costs, while travel and festival food remain the main extras.

videos.title: Muck n' Mac Fest 2022
videos.description:
Feast your eyes upon the Muck n’ Mac Fest 2022 after movie, courtesy of @six4productions!

After a couple cancellations through Covid, it was an absolute pleasure to finally deliver the festival at Traquair House… Aaand what a setting it was! Thank-you so much for having us @traquair House!

Our thanks also goes out to Event Scotland, the support we’ve had on the National Events Programme has been invaluable and helped us deliver the exact vision we’ve had in mind over these past few years. 

Also, to our amazing event partners both local and further afield – your support has truly helped sculpt the event into a cracker, that’s hopefully here to stay for many years to come!

No event like this is possible without the help of an amazing team of volunteers, thank-you so much – it really means the world to a small company that’s on the way up!

Lastly, so thankful to all our attendees who joined us in 2022. We’re really grateful for all your constructive feedback in our post-event forms, we’ve read through comments meticulously and already have plans underway to go beyond your expectations for the second edition. 

See you in 2023?

videos.title: Muck n' Mac Fest Teaser
videos.description:
Muck n' Mac Fest 29th April - 1st May 2022. 

Staged in the grounds of Scotland's oldest inhabited Home, Traquair House will host the inaugural festival in 2022.

Nestled in the heart of the Tweed Valley, Traquair just so happens to be the gateway to some of the finest gravel riding the country has to offer! 

Over the course of the weekend, riders will take on 6 timed stages, which are accumulated in a GC format for the overall. In between, the clock stops running, giving riders the opportunity to kick back, have a blether and take in the rolling hills of the Borders that surround. 

The weekend is as much about riding as the time off the bike. Our festival village has an amazing mix of activities on offer. Expect to see; live music, film, event partner expo, camping, yoga, bar areas, mixed catering experiences and various family friendly activities around the grounds of the house.

videos.title: Behind the scenes in the bike industry at Muck n Mac gravel cycling event and race
videos.description:
Ever wondered what us industry bods do whilst you're out racing at events? May 2025 saw Muck n Mac kick off the GrAlba Series of gravel cycling races and Grinduro Scotland. I went along to represent Bridgedale - one of my bike industry clients - and speak to riders and event organisers as well as network with some bike industry friends.

Much more to come to the channel from more behind the scenes videos to race videos, Hyrox, The Gralloch, Sarn Helen challenge, Grinduro, Gritfest and much more as well as more about living life without limits and life without number as we aim for World Champs qualifying in UCI gravel and Hyrox fitness racing.

This channel is dedicated to all those people 45+ (or approaching the age milestone) who think their best fitness years are behind them. Join me and together we will prove that wrong! Life is for adventure and to move. Experience it all, age is just a number. Live #lifewithoutnumber Life starts here!

Thanks for watching folks! 

I am a bike industry professional of many years but al products here are bought by me and are not clients. I will always say when a product featured is a client of mine. No BS. It's the way I live and honesty is the very least anyone deserves in life.
